prompt: Merchant can manually trigger bulk image optimization of product and collection images down to 400x400 pixels and see detailed results.

intent.desiredOutcome: Merchant can manually trigger bulk image optimization of product and collection images down to 400x400 pixels and see detailed results.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version handles images at different aspect ratios gracefully (resize vs. crop decisions should be consistent and documented). The detailed results page must clearly show which images succeeded and which failed, with actionable error messages. The app should avoid re-optimizing already-optimized images on subsequent runs. Performance matters — if the store has thousands of images, the run should show progress or allow the merchant to understand why it takes time. Edge cases: animated images (GIFs), WebP formats, and missing source files should be handled explicitly.

plan.dataFlow: A merchant clicks 'Start Optimization' in the admin panel, which creates a new optimization run record in the pending state and immediately transitions it to processing. The system bulk-fetches all product and collection images from the catalog, then for each image checks whether a prior run already succeeded for that image's external identifier; images with a prior success are recorded as skipped. For each remaining image the system resizes it to fit within 400×400 pixels while preserving aspect ratio, writes the optimized version back to the catalog, and records the per-image outcome as succeeded or failed with a descriptive reason. Once all images are processed the run transitions to completed (or failed if a systemic error prevented completion), and the merchant can view the detailed results page filtered by run, showing counts and per-image outcomes with actionable error messages.

capabilities.description: Fetch all product images from the catalog for the current store.
Fetch all collection images from the catalog for the current store.
Determine which images were successfully optimized in a prior run and should be skipped.
Resize a single image to fit within 400×400 pixels while preserving its aspect ratio.
Upload the resized image and associate it with its parent product or collection, replacing the original.
Persist the per-image result — succeeded, failed, or skipped — with a descriptive reason for any non-success.
Transition the optimization run to its terminal state and record aggregate counts once all images are processed.
Return a summary list of all past optimization runs with their aggregate outcomes for the admin panel.
Return the full per-image result records for a specific optimization run.

persistence.name: optimization_run
persistence.purpose: Tracks each merchant-triggered bulk optimization job and its aggregate outcome.

columns.name: total_count
columns.purpose: total number of images discovered for this run

columns.name: skipped_count
columns.purpose: images skipped because they were already optimized

persistence.keyedBy: one row per optimization run, keyed by its internal identifier

persistence.name: image_result
persistence.purpose: Records the per-image outcome for every image processed within an optimization run.

columns.name: run_id
columns.purpose: the optimization run this result belongs to

columns.name: image_external_id
columns.purpose: the catalog's stable identifier for this image

columns.name: resource_type
columns.purpose: whether the image belongs to a product or a collection

columns.name: resource_external_id
columns.purpose: the catalog's stable identifier for the parent product or collection

columns.name: resource_title
columns.purpose: human-readable name of the parent product or collection at processing time

columns.name: outcome
columns.purpose: whether this image succeeded, failed, or was skipped

columns.name: reason
columns.purpose: actionable description of why the image failed or was skipped

columns.name: original_width
columns.purpose: pixel width of the source image before optimization

columns.name: original_height
columns.purpose: pixel height of the source image before optimization

persistence.keyedBy: one row per image per optimization run, keyed by the combination of run identifier and image external identifier

transitions.trigger: all images have been evaluated and outcomes recorded
a systemic error prevents the run from continuing

invariants: a run in 'completed' or 'failed' never returns to 'pending' or 'processing'
only one run may be in the 'processing' state at any given time
every image discovered during a run must have exactly one image_result row for that run before the run transitions to 'completed'

externalContracts.purpose: Trigger a new bulk image optimization run.
List all past optimization runs with their summary counts and status.
Return the detailed per-image results for a specific optimization run.

edgeCases: An image is an animated GIF — it must be skipped and the reason recorded as 'animated images cannot be safely resized', never silently corrupted.
An image source URL is unreachable or returns no content at processing time — record the outcome as failed with the HTTP status or connectivity error as the reason.
An image already succeeded in a prior run — it must be skipped in the current run to prevent redundant writes and catalog churn.
A new run is requested while another run is already in the processing state — reject the request immediately and return a clear message that a run is already in progress.
An image's original dimensions are already within 400×400 pixels — it must be skipped rather than re-encoded, with the reason recorded as 'already within target dimensions'.
A WebP image is encountered — it must be processed identically to JPEG and PNG with no special-case failure, as the resize logic must treat media type as advisory only.
